grh_003e40792b92681bdc14.title: Improvisation
paragraphs: Struggling actor Tom needs money before his pregnant wife gives birth, and his unusual ability to use yoga to make himself appear dead gives his actor friends a dangerous idea. They propose reinstating his life-insurance policy, faking his death, obtaining a false certificate and substituting a dummy before burial so his wife can collect the proceeds. Their elaborate improvisation unravels amid a locked mortuary, a damaged dummy, suspicious professionals and a farcical legal confrontation. The fraud never becomes the easy solution they imagined. Instead, the mortician offers Tom legitimate flexible work driving a hearse, a job he can leave when acting work appears, giving him a practical way to support his family without pretending to die.

grh_0088a63590c118b849f9.title: My Hero
paragraphs: Newly promoted network employee Cathy Applebee falls for celebrated foreign correspondent David Jeffries, who claims he is dying of cancer and uses the story to persuade her to move in and care for him. In private David boasts that the illness is a scam, while at home he belittles Cathy, pressures her to abandon her own work, and invokes his supposed condition whenever she resists him. After the deception is exposed and David loses his position, he tries to charm Cathy into persuading her boss to rehire him. Cathy refuses both the relationship and the favor, telling him that pity cannot sustain love and that his deeper sickness is the way he manipulates people.

grh_00bc07ad62a1881f4d50.title: Two Notes
paragraphs: Dr. Christian tells Judy about elderly neurologist Dr. Tuxbury, who has become convinced that his noisy upstairs tenant James Burton hates him and proudly describes what he believes is a perfect murder. Using a metronome and two repeated piano notes, Tuxbury claims he can exploit Burton's fear and heart response until the man's pulse races beyond endurance. The demonstration appears to work and Burton collapses, but the supposed victim has already recognized Tuxbury's growing paranoia and deliberately stages the reactions Tuxbury expects. No murder has taken place. Tuxbury is eventually confined to the state institution for the criminally insane, where he still reenacts his imaginary perfect crime for anyone willing to listen.
